findings.title: Reintroduction of CVE-2026-113733: Password hash disclosure to view-only admin users with custom user models
findings.description: This diff reverts the fix for CVE-2026-113733. The original code in `django/contrib/admin/utils.py` checked whether a `password` field belonged to any `AbstractBaseUser` subclass (or a model related to the auth user model via inheritance), ensuring password hashes were rendered as masked hashes (`render_password_as_hash`) for all user-like models. The new code narrows the check to `field.model == get_user_model()`, which only matches the exact `AUTH_USER_MODEL` class. As documented in the removed CVE text, this reintroduces the vulnerability: admin users with view-only permission to a custom user model (not set as `AUTH_USER_MODEL`, or inheriting `password` via multi-table inheritance from a concrete parent) will again be shown the full password hash. The accompanying tests (`test_password_display_for_field_inherited_user_model`, `test_password_display_for_field_user_model_not_abstract_base_user`, `test_password_display_for_field_other_user_model`) and test models (`ParentUser`, `ChildUser`, `MinimalPasswordUser`) that validated the fix are also deleted, removing regression coverage. This is a direct security regression that exposes sensitive credential material (password hashes) to users who should not see them, enabling offline cracking attacks.
